The symplastic pathway involves movement through plasmodesmata without crossing plasma membranes. Sucrose from mesophyll cells moves symplastically into the phloem via the bundle sheath, phloem parenchyma, companion cells, and finally into sieve tubes.  
Option (A) starts with fibers, which are not part of this symplastic route.  
Option (B) includes tracheids (xylem, not phloem) and incorrect order.  
Option (C) starts with companion cells, but companion cells are near the end of the pathway, not the beginning.  
Option (D) correctly follows: bundle sheath → phloem parenchyma → companion cell → sieve tube.  

Final answer: (D)
